outline: 1133 Area of a Triangle using Trigonometry

examples.question_text: Solve $\cos\theta=\dfrac{8^{2}+10^{2}-12^{2}}{2(8)(10)}$, giving $\theta$ to the nearest minute.
A triangular frame has sides $6$ m, $8$ m and $11$ m. Find its largest angle, correct to $1$ decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
The largest angle is opposite the longest side, $11$ m, so take $c=11$.
$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\dfrac{a^{2}+b^{2}-c^{2}}{2ab}\\\cos\theta&=\dfrac{6^{2}+8^{2}-11^{2}}{2(6)(8)}\\\cos\theta&=-\dfrac{21}{96}\\\theta&=\cos^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{21}{96}\right)\\\theta&\approx102.6^{\circ}\end{align*}$
The negative cosine gives an obtuse angle.

examples.question_text: A triangle has side lengths $5$ cm, $12$ cm and $13$ cm. Use the cosine rule to find the angle opposite the $13$ cm side, correct to $2$ decimal places.

methods.description: Apply inverse cosine to a supplied equation and convert the decimal part of the angle to minutes when requested.

examples.derivation: (64+100−144)/160=0.125. Inverse cosine gives 82.8192442185°. The decimal part gives 49.1546531 minutes, so the answer is 82°49′. No diagram is necessary.

AC is opposite B. cos B=(49+64−81)/112=2/7, giving B=73.398450401°≈73.40°. Diagram lengths BA=3.5, BC≈4 and AC≈4.5 consistently represent 7, 8 and 9 cm. The marked angle is at B; the answer and side-role annotations appear only in the solution.

The largest angle is opposite 11 m. cos θ=(36+64−121)/96=−21/96, giving θ=102.635625093°≈102.6°. The negative cosine correctly identifies an obtuse angle. The explicit side-length prompt is sufficient without a diagram.
For the angle opposite 13 cm, cos θ=(25+144−169)/120=0. Therefore θ=90.00°. This uses the same source-taught cosine-rule method; no diagram is necessary.
